common_name: Bloom-A-Thon Hot Pink Azalea (Reblooming Compact Vivid Pink Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade to morning sun; Bloom-A-Thon Hot Pink reblooms continuously from spring through fall rather than in a few discrete flushes and tolerates more sun than most traditional azaleas.

directions: Bloom-A-Thon Hot Pink carries vivid, saturated hot-pink flowers on a compact, naturally mounded shrub, part of a breeding series developed as an alternative to the Encore line with a more continuously repeating bloom pattern through the growing season rather than distinct spring, summer, and fall flushes. Its tidy habit needs little pruning to stay in shape, and like other Bloom-A-Thon selections it tolerates considerably more direct sun than older azalea types once established, extending its usefulness beyond the deep shade typically required for reliable azalea bloom. Plant in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to morning sun, water deeply during dry spells to support the extended bloom cycle, and prune lightly right after the heaviest spring flush to avoid removing developing buds for later color.

directions: Bloom-A-Thon Lavender carries soft lavender-purple flowers on a compact, naturally mounded shrub, offering a cooler-toned option within the Bloom-A-Thon series that pairs easily with pinks, blues, and white companion plantings. Like its siblings in the line it reblooms nearly continuously through the growing season rather than flowering only in short flushes, and its tidy habit needs little pruning to hold shape. Plant in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to morning sun, water deeply during dry spells to support the extended bloom cycle, and prune lightly right after the heaviest spring flush to avoid removing developing buds for later color.

It shares the series' hallmark near-continuous rebloom through the growing season rather than a few short flushes, and its tidy habit needs little pruning to hold shape. Plant in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to morning sun, water deeply during dry spells to support the extended bloom cycle, and prune lightly right after the heaviest spring flush to avoid removing developing buds for later color.

common_name: Perfecto Mundo Hot Pink Azalea (Reblooming Sun-Tolerant Compact Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; Perfecto Mundo was bred for particularly strong sun tolerance and reliable rebloom, making it a good option for a bed that gets more direct light than azaleas traditionally prefer.

directions: Perfecto Mundo Hot Pink is a compact, reblooming azalea bred as a Proven Winners ColorChoice introduction with an emphasis on strong sun tolerance and dense, well-branched growth, producing vivid hot-pink flowers in flushes from spring through fall rather than the single spring bloom of traditional azaleas. Its compact size and tidy, mounded habit suit foundation plantings and mixed containers, and it needs minimal pruning to hold shape through the season. Plant in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil, giving it more direct sun than older azalea types tolerate, and water deeply during dry spells to sustain the extended bloom cycle; light pruning right after the heaviest spring flush avoids removing developing buds for later color.

Plant in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil, giving it more direct sun than older azalea types tolerate, and water deeply during dry spells to sustain the extended bloom cycle; light pruning right after the heaviest spring flush avoids removing developing buds for later color.
